leads.claim: dbbi (91) parsed left-to-right with b and g as two-character prefixes gives exactly 64 tokens with exactly 16 distinct codes (a ba bb be bf bh c d e f gb ge gg gi h i). The claim is that it could be a substituted SHA-256 hex digest. The equality pattern (labels by first occurrence) is 01234556728966286abc61c88b48de3086dd501d5557d6bab5605233df7bbb96. b/g is said to be the only prefix pair of 36 that gives 64/16; shuffle control 0.3% (post hoc).
leads.method: prefix-parse; compare isomorphism pattern of sha256(candidate) hex
leads.self_verifying_note: If any candidate's sha256 hex has the same 64-position equality pattern, that is ~impossible by chance, so the mapping recovers itself. It works as a judge for matrixsumlist serializations. The 64/16 parse count was reproduced here.
leads.status: open; overlaps our b/be prime-position finding
leads.novelty: medium (pattern-match harness is new to us)

leads.claim: A 'cosmic_correct' Cosmic Duality decryption yields a list of addresses ('12addrs'; chat: output of GitHub issue #110 construction).
leads.method: own base58check parse; entropy of the claimed plaintext
leads.result_here: The file is 39 valid P2PKH addresses (not 12), and the prize address is not among them. The 'verified' Cosmic plaintext is 1327 B with 7.87 bit/byte entropy and 39% printable bytes, which is a PKCS#7 0x01 padding false positive (~1/256 per password). Any derived address list is noise.

leads.claim: SalPhaseIon segments alternate with the Architect speech. Even segments sit at speech lines. Odd segments (matrixsumlist, lastwordsbeforearchichoice, thispassword, shabef..., enter, 'sha bef ans too') stand where the creator skipped Architect/Neo lines. So 'shabefanstoo' = sha256 the (skipped) answer too.

leads.claim: Split dbbi and faed into (a) the stream with doubled letters removed and (b) the doubled-letter stream (dbbi doubles 'bbccggbbhhhhffbbccceeggffeee'; faed doubles 'ggeehhggddaagggg...').
leads.note: Deterministic transform, but only readable output would validate it. Doubled letters in faed are mostly g (the 'g = two digit values' observation in cycle 37).

leads.claim: Hypothesis: dbbi_91 (7x13) / faed_570 (15x38) are directed knight's walks, with letters mapped injectively to the 8 knight offsets.
leads.self_verifying_note: A legal non-revisiting (Hamiltonian) walk under one global injective map would be very unlikely by chance. A quick prefilter rejects maps where adjacent letter pairs map to inverse offsets. No result in the doc.

leads.claim: (a) The Phase 3.2 plaintext (2,422 B) splits on CRLF-CRLF into six fields of 332/107/1539/149/... bytes. (b) The creator swapped the film's '23 individuals, 16 female, 7 male' into '23 ciphers, 16 encryptions, 7 passwords'. (c) DBBI selection witness: L=84 parse (61-symbol residue) vs L=83, argued from creator hints 'first or zero', '{1},{4},{21}', 'R=18 A=1 B=2 / could also be 21 or 1812 bit' -> byte 21 bit 4 (FE cell). (d) 'zero-width letters of DBBI's yellow suffixes over the 23-word message spell N I I L'.
leads.note: Structural parse claims can be checked deterministically. None of them is a password-producing result. Most useful as a ledger of what another lab closed.
